proof:
# Convexity and exact quadrature for affine simplex-chain caps

This lemma is dimension-independent but concerns the specified affine
common-vertex simplex family. It is not a general mixed-integer theorem.

Let d>=1, T=conv(0,e_1,...,e_d), V=1/d!, u_i>=0, sum u_i=1, and

    F_r(s)=|rT intersect {u.x>=s}|/V.

Normalize the central radius to one and put t=1/(d+1). Let k>0 and
0<=beta<kt. For 0<=h<=1/k define r=1-kh and the two actual cap functions

    f_-(h)=F_r(t-beta h),
    f_+(h)=F_r(t+beta(h+1)).

Extend both by zero for h>=1/k. Then both are convex functions on
[0,infinity). In particular, for either function f,

    sum_(h=0)^infinity f(h) >= integral_0^infinity f(x)dx + f(0)/2,
    sum_(h=0)^infinity f(h) >= f(0).

All sums are finite. If 0<k<=1, their convex combination gives

    sum f(h) >= (1-k) integral f + (1+k)f(0)/2.           (1)

## Proof retaining the exact facet law

Let Theta be uniform on the opposite facet of T and U=u.Theta.
For s>0, radial integration gives the exact identity

    F_r(s)=E[(r^d-(s/U)^d)_+],                           (2)

where the integrand is defined as zero when U=0. This convention is
also its limiting value; the thresholds below are strictly positive.
The identity holds for a constant projection as well as an atomless one.

Write c=beta/k<t. In terms of r in[0,1], the left threshold is

    s_-(r)=t-c+cr,

and the right threshold is

    s_+(r)=t+beta+c-cr.

For a fixed U>0, consider g(r)=(r^d-(s(r)/U)^d)_+ on[0,1].
For the left threshold its active interval, if nonempty, is

    r>(t-c)/(U-c),

which requires U>c. For the right threshold its active interval is

    r>(t+beta+c)/(U+c).

If that interval meets[0,1], then U>t+beta>c. Thus U>c holds in every
nonempty active interval of either integrand.

For d>=2, within an active interval the second derivative is

    g''(r)=d(d-1)[r^(d-2)-c^2 s(r)^(d-2)/U^d].

Since s(r)<Ur there, this is at least

    d(d-1)r^(d-2)(1-c^2/U^2)>0.

At the activation radius r_0>0, the right derivative is
d r_0^(d-1)(1-c/U) for the left threshold, and
d r_0^(d-1)(1+c/U) for the right threshold. Both are positive, whereas
the derivative on the zero interval is zero. Hence there is an upward
derivative jump and each integrand is convex on[0,1]. For d=1 the
active expression is affine and the same positive derivative jump
proves convexity directly. If there is no active interval the
integrand is identically zero. The case U=0 is also identically zero.

Expectations preserve convexity, so (2) gives convexity in r and hence
in h under the affine reversal r=1-kh. Both thresholds stay uniformly
positive, while max U<=1. Therefore both cap functions vanish on a
whole neighborhood to the left of h=1/k. Extending by zero preserves
convexity on[0,infinity); no endpoint derivative assumption is needed.

Integrating the convex trapezoid inequality on each unit interval
and summing gives integral f <= sum f-f(0)/2. The other bound is the
nonnegative first summand. Combining them with weights1-k and k proves
(1). The derivation involves no approximation of the lattice sum by an
integral: it is a one-sided inequality with its exact endpoint term.

## Explicit integrals for later angular work

The following formulas retain U as the exact simplex-facet projection.
They do not replace its law by an arbitrary fixed-mean distribution.
Assume c>0 and put B=t+beta. From(2) and Tonelli,

    integral f_- = E[J_-(U)]/[k(d+1)],
    integral f_+ = E[J_+(U)]/[k(d+1)],

where J_-(U)=0 for U<=t, J_+(U)=0 for U<=B, and otherwise

    J_-(U)=1-t^(d+1)/(c U^d)+(t-c)^(d+1)/(c(U-c)^d),
    J_+(U)=1+B^(d+1)/(c U^d)-(B+c)^(d+1)/(c(U+c)^d).

These follow by integrating the two active radial powers between their
activation radius and one; all denominators are positive on the
indicated domains. For c=0, each integral is the expectation of

    [1-(d+1)(t/U)^d+d(t/U)^(d+1)]_+ /[k(d+1)]

with the bracket formula used ONLY for U>t, and zero otherwise.
Equivalently one can take the displayed integral directly at c=0;
there is no need to interchange a singular formula and a limit.

The outstanding question is a sharp lower bound for the resulting
Dirichlet expectations for all u. This lemma alone does not establish
that bound or the mixed-integer center guarantee.
